newsitem.title: USA: Trial begins in Florida for accused serial killer.
newsitem.headline: Trial begins in Florida for accused serial killer.

text.p: Jury selection began Monday in the murder trial of Glen Rogers, a drifter charged in the deaths of four women during a cross-country killing spree in 1995.

Prosecutors in California, Mississippi, Louisiana and Florida accused Rogers, a 34-year-old native of Hamilton, Ohio, of charming women he in met in bars into moving in with him or giving him rides home.

He was captured in Kentucky in November 1995 but sent to Florida to stand trial because prosecutors believed they had a strong case against him in the death of Tina Cribbs, 34, a maid and mother of two who was killed after meeting Rogers at a bar.
Authorities also said Rogers killed Sandra Gallagher in Van Nuys, California, Linda Price in Jackson, Mississippi, and Andy Sutton in Bossier City, Louisiana, between September and November 1995.
In addition, Kentucky authorities now want to talk to Rogers about the 1993 death of Mark Peters, 71, who had let Rogers share his home.

At the start of jury selection Monday, Hillsborough County Circuit Judge Diana Allen asked potential jurors in a packed courtroom: "If any of you, for personal or religions reasons, are opposed to the imposition of the death penalty?"
A dozen hands went up. Allen then asked if any of those people would be unable to set aside, at least temporarily, their views. No hands went down.
Names were taken and jury selection continued.
Opening arguments were expected to begin Wednesday and the trial was expected to last two weeks.

Rogers was captured in Kentucky two days after Cribbs' body was found in a blood-spattered Tampa motel room. He was by then on the FBI's most-wanted list and was driving Cribbs' white Ford Fiesta when he was caught after a high-speed chase.
